incumbent.name: Jerry Goodin
incumbent.summary: Jerry Goodin, a former Indiana State Police trooper, ran for sheriff as a Democrat in 2018 and took office in 2019 {wdrb_2018} {scso_jail_2023}. He remains sheriff as of September 2026 and is not on the 2026 ballot {ct_scam} {in_list}; a sheriff who has served since 2019 has reached the limit of eight years in any twelve-year period.
record: 2018 campaign: Goodin, then a nearly 27-year Indiana State Police trooper at the Sellersburg post, said he would make drug dealers a top priority while offering education and job training to jailed addicts, and supported school resource officers on every campus as part of a broader school safety plan {wdrb_2018}.

2019–2023: The sheriff's office says Goodin prioritized in-house jail operations on taking office and that the Scott County Jail passed the annual state jail inspection four years in a row through March 2023, after not passing in over 20 years {scso_jail_2022} {scso_jail_2023}.
2020–2022: The Indiana Sheriffs' Association named Goodin Indiana Sheriff of the Year for 2020 and 2022 (and all 92 sheriffs for 2021), according to the sheriff's office {scso_soty_2022}.

race_context: This is an open seat: Sheriff Jerry Goodin, in office since 2019, is not on the ballot {scso_jail_2023} {in_list}.

Both nominees filed on the first day of the filing period in January 2026 {ct_filing}. In the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, Scott Zellers won with 1,089 votes to 425 for Shawn S. Mayer; Democrat Joe Guarneri was unopposed {ct_primary}.
Guarneri is the sheriff's chief deputy under Sheriff Goodin {ct_aed} {ct_scam}.
Local coverage of the general-election campaign is very thin: no candidate questionnaires, forums or debates were found.

candidates.summary: Joe Guarneri is chief deputy of the Scott County Sheriff's Office under Sheriff Jerry Goodin; he is the Democratic nominee {ct_aed} {ct_primary}.
background: Chief deputy of the Scott County Sheriff's Office as of 2026 {ct_aed} {ct_scam}; identified as Lt. Colonel in a September 2024 sheriff's office release and in a March 2023 jail-inspection photo caption {scso_youth_2024} {scso_jail_2023}.
In September 2024 he spoke with first-grade students visiting the courthouse about friendship and safety, saying officers should reach out to children whenever they can {scso_youth_2024}.
path_to_ballot: Filed for sheriff as a Democrat on the first day of the January 2026 filing period {ct_filing}.
Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {ct_primary}; listed on the general-election ballot as a Democrat {in_list}.

items: In June 2026, as chief deputy, said that because deputies are often first to arrive at emergencies in rural parts of the county, carrying defibrillators in patrol cars makes sense {ct_aed}.
